<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s).

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-driven.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation-rules.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/deployment/troubleshooting.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/quick-reference.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/backward-compatibility.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/concept.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 24b6ae55016b74c4bcef81f09cdaa4684ffc9423` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c18c806474cdef99dddeb54c6eae08c669f8fdcf` — the merge of head `7f7310830a0d4fa73576d316afafc25dbb134b2d` into base `24b6ae55016b74c4bcef81f09cdaa4684ffc9423`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c18c806474cdef99dddeb54c6eae08c669f8fdcf && git checkout c18c806474cdef99dddeb54c6eae08c669f8fdcf
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 24b6ae55016b74c4bcef81f09cdaa4684ffc9423 7f7310830a0d4fa73576d316afafc25dbb134b2d && git checkout -B drift-repro 24b6ae55016b74c4bcef81f09cdaa4684ffc9423 && git merge --no-ff 7f7310830a0d4fa73576d316afafc25dbb134b2d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 24b6ae55016b74c4bcef81f09cdaa4684ffc9423
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 24b6ae55016b74c4bcef81f09cdaa4684ffc9423` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7f7310830a0d4fa73576d316afafc25dbb134b2d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.lookup-filter-record-path-multi-valued-refused.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-object-field-refs.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-object-field-refs.test.ts (narrowing floor, all in the diff); read, not reviewed: packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts (`isMultiValueField`, `MULTI_CAPABLE_TYPES`), packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts (`GraphField`, `graphFieldOf`, `resolveFieldPath`), ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/lookupRecordReference.ts (`readRecordPath`, `resolveLookupFilters`), packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.lookup-filter-record-path-unknown-refused.ts (the template entry), card #34389 (the client half the jsdoc cites)

Inputs read: card #34378 body and all 9 comments, PR #34489 body, file list and 2 comments, the net diff from merge-base `e8cba8fe` to the head (7 files, +218/-8), the 68 check-runs on the head, and the log of the one failed shard. No path this diff touches differs between the merge-base and current `main`.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set, narrowed, right. `object-field-ref-unknown` at `lookupFilters[N].value.$record` now also refuses a path that resolves when (a) its first segment is an authored multi-valued field of the owning object, whether the path ends there or hops through it, or (b) its leaf behind a single-valued hop is an authored multi-valued field. Read in `validate-object-field-refs.ts`: the check runs only when `judge` reported nothing (`!hit`) and only on the one slot carrying `singleValued`, so no other member of the family changes verdict, and a path the family already refuses gets one finding, never two (pinned by the misspelt-leaf case).
- Predicate, right. `multiValuedSegment` calls spec's `isMultiValueField` with the graph slice's `type` and `multiple === true`; `graphFieldOf` carries `multiple` as true or undefined, so the call is exact. No second copy of the type list enters lint.
- Unjudged cases, right and as declared. An injected head is not in `fields` and is skipped; an injected leaf is skipped by `verdict.injected`; a leaf on an object outside the stack is `unknowable` and skipped; a multi-valued head whose target is outside the stack is still refused, because the head is the owning object's own field (pinned by `partners.anything` and `watchers.department`).
- Parse accept-set, unchanged, right. `LookupFilterRecordReferenceSchema` and its path regex are untouched; only two `.describe` strings and one jsdoc paragraph change in `field.zod.ts`. The parse still accepts the spelling; the refusal is lint's, which is what both describes say.
- Public surface, right. One new ADR-0087 semantic entry id, `lookup-filter-record-path-multi-valued-refused`; no id collision at the head or on current `main`. The regenerated `field.mdx` rows match the two describes word for word.
- Consumers, unchanged. The rule still reaches `os lint` / `os validate` / `os build`, the metadata doors and the publish receipt probe through the same exports (`reference-integrity-suite.ts`, `authoring-rules.ts`, `build-probes.ts`); the diff adds a finding to an existing rule at its existing severity, so the changeset's list of doors is the rule's existing wiring and not a new claim.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `@objectstack/lint: minor`, `@objectstack/spec: minor`, with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on both the PR body and the changeset, a BREAKING paragraph, FROM/TO and a fix. This matches what the diff publishes: lint refuses metadata it accepted before (a narrowing, carried as minor under the repo's no-major rule), and spec publishes new describe text plus one semantic entry. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- The `Clause-②` sentence is accurate against the tree: first segment or leaf, the three picker field types, error severity, and "reported, never refused" on the receipt probe.
- The exposure claim (zero first-party `$record` paths) is the dev's measurement; nothing in the diff or the green lint and dogfood gate families contradicts it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- open_questions 1 (contract review needed): answered by this record.
- open_questions 2 (Test Core red): read. Check-run `Test Core (3/8)` failed in step `@objectstack/mcp#test`; first error line: `FAIL src/mcp-file-tools.test.ts - read_file extracts PDF and Word text on a worker pool, off the request thread - out of CPU budget on the worker: the pages read so far, truncated, with the budget note, as in-process`, `AssertionError` at `src/mcp-file-tools.test.ts:950:19` (expected `content: "text"`, `truncated: true`; received `content: "none"`), 1 failed of 1226. The aggregate `Test Core` check is red for that shard alone; the other seven shards are green. It does not touch this diff: no file under `packages/mcp` is changed, the failing assertion is a CPU-budget timing reading on a PDF worker, and the diff's spec half is describe text plus a migration entry that the test does not read. By reading it is unrelated; it is NOT cleared here. The head still carries a red required check, and it needs a re-run of that job (or a fresh head) before landing. Option A of the dev's question stands.
- open_questions 3 (describe wording, "is not resolved"): answered in ④ as N1; option A, keep as ruled.
- Dev deviations: the attribution lines ahead of `Fixes #34378` and the dev-run dogfood battery are process matters for the lane seat, with no contract effect.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The change is a pure in-memory judgment over the authored stack; no query, no id materialisation, no in-app join.
- Skills-docs follow-up #34201: accepted as declared; no skill or hand-written doc teaches `$record` in this diff's reach.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Narrowing face. Read against the published spec on `main`: the `$record` comparand is declared as one value of the edited record, paired only with the six scalar comparisons, never a member of an `in` / `notIn` list. A multi-valued field holds an array by the spec's own value contract (`isMultiValueField` decides `z.array(element)`), so a path through or to one never had a declared single value. The refusal makes the spec's own limit real at authoring; it takes no declared capability away. Nothing was declared and left undelivered: the card measured both shapes as already broken in the picker (a hop is left out silently, a plain path sends the list under a scalar operator), confirmed here in `readRecordPath`.

`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`. The jsdoc and both describes state the same rule with the same field classes, and name `isMultiValueField` as the definition. "One flagged `multiple: true`, or a multiselect, checkboxes or tags field" agrees with the predicate on every stack that parses, since `FieldSchema` refuses `multiple: true` outside the multi-capable types and on `radio`. Its first consumer, the lint member, implements exactly these three shapes.

`18.lookup-filter-record-path-multi-valued-refused.ts`. Surface, replacement, reason and acceptance criteria agree with the code sentence by sentence: the doors and loaders are the template entry's, the two refused shapes match `multiValuedSegment`, "not judged" matches the injected and out-of-stack skips, and "no mechanical rewrite" is honest. The reason states the client's present behaviour for both shapes correctly.

`packages/lint/src/validate-object-field-refs.ts`. Attempts to break it, all held: a two-hop path returns before the check; a hop through a non-relationship multi-valued field (`tags.x`) is already a miss, reported once; a multi-valued head with a misspelt leaf is reported once as the miss; `multiple: false` and an absent flag read as single; a leaf reached through an injected hop is `unknowable` and skipped; the head lookup reads authored fields only, as the slot's docblock says. The header docblock, the slot docblock and the message agree with the code.

`packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`. The added sentences match the three shapes and the reason; the one-line-verdict fact list pins the phrase.

`packages/lint/src/validate-object-field-refs.test.ts`. Six refusals each pin severity, rule, path and hint (three pin the full message), one pins the single finding on a miss, and one control set covers a plain field, a single lookup, a single hop, a `multiple: false` select and an injected-column leaf. The dev's ablation reading (exactly the six refusals fail) fits the shape of the guard.

N1 (nit) — "it is not resolved" in the two describes is true today of the hop shape only; for a plain path to a non-empty multi-valued field the picker on `main` still sends the list (`readRecordPath` returns the collapsed value, `resolveLookupFilters` pushes it). Card #34378 Expected item 2 rules this clause in these words and splits the client half to #34389, which is open, in the ui queue, and named in the jsdoc. Lint now refuses such a path at every door and measured exposure is zero, so no authored stack reaches the gap through a gated route. Accepted deviation, carried by #34389; no change on this head.

Observation outside the card, not a finding on this diff: a `$record` path to a structured field (json, repeater, location, address, vector) also yields no scalar and is not judged by this predicate. The card scopes the rule to multi-valued fields; a follow-up card may weigh it.

## 席位核对

**L1 verdict: ACCEPT** · card #34378 · area o2-A · first review · read at 2026-11-16T23:59Z
Head-sha: `7f7310830a0d4fa73576d316afafc25dbb134b2d` (the final head announced in comment 6933122514)

Checklist, read against GitHub and `origin/main`, not against the report:

- **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, `mergeable_state: clean`. The first card line is `Fixes #34378`, and a closing-keyword scan of the whole body finds no other match. `Fixes` is right: the card carries only the spec + lint half. The client half was split to #34389 (open, `domain:ui`), and that split is recorded on #34389 ("#34378 now carries only the lint + describe half") and in the spec seat's delta. No `ui/` file is in the diff.
- **File surface** (`get_files`, 7 files, +218/-8): `packages/lint/src/validate-object-field-refs.ts`, its test, `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` (describes and jsdoc only), the new ADR-0087 semantic entry `18.lookup-filter-record-path-multi-valued-refused.ts`, the regenerated `content/docs/references/data/field.mdx`, and `.changeset/34378-…md`. This is the delta's surface. The `field.mdx` change is generated, not hand-edited: its two rows match the two describes word for word, and `Lint & Repo Gates`, which carries `check:generated`, is `success`. No `content/docs/releases/` change.
- **Resumed commits.** `ff1bf727`, `5b520173` and `3781dec5` came from a stopped thread with no report. The body says every reading was re-taken on this branch, and the tests and ablation below are at this head.
- **Changeset.** Both `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/spec` publish, at `minor` with a **BREAKING** paragraph, FROM → TO and a Fix line. The ADR-0087 registration marker names the new entry. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` and `Skills-docs: follow-up #34201` sit at line start in both the body and the changeset, and #34201 is open with the matching scope. I checked its prose sentence by sentence:
  - "`{ $record: "accounts.cb_market" }` through a `multiple: true` lookup, or `{ $record: "tags" }`, linted clean": true on base. The member judged names only.
  - "now refuses the path at the multi-valued field and names it": matches the pinned messages `names "tags"` / `goes through "accounts"` / `ends at "markets"`.
  - "Multi-valued means `isMultiValueField` …": the lint calls spec's predicate and adds no second type list.
  - "A registry-injected column and a leaf on an object outside the stack are not judged": the injected-column-leaf control is clean, while the out-of-stack *head* case is refused, as worded ("leaf").
  - "Measured first-party exposure: zero": the body gives the `git grep` reading with a positive control (8 lines in the test file).
- **Tests and evidence.** A new block of 8 cases.
  - Six refusals, each asserting `severity: 'error'`, `rule: OBJECT_FIELD_REF_UNKNOWN`, the finding path and the hint; three pin the full message.
  - One case pins the miss-once behaviour, and one control set stays clean: plain single, single lookup, single hop, `multiple: false` select, and an injected-column leaf.
  - These are lint findings, not HTTP refusals, so ADR-0112 `code`/`status` does not apply; the lint finding's own `rule` + `severity` are asserted.
  - Ablation (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, cardinality read guarded off): `Tests 6 failed | 121 passed (127)`, exactly the six refusals; restored blob `fd916767` == HEAD.
  - Forced test edits are named in the body: a `markets: multiselect` field on the shared fixture that no existing case reads, and one new phrase in the verdict-fact list. Nothing is loosened.
- **Gates (check-runs at `7f731083`, `filter=latest`, 68 runs).** 58 `success`, 10 path-filtered `skipped`, none red or pending.
  - Required floor: Lint & Repo Gates `success`, TypeScript Type Check `success`.
  - `Test Core` aggregate `success`, with shards 1–8/8 all `success`. Shard 3/8's first attempt failed on `@objectstack/mcp` `mcp-file-tools.test.ts:950`, a 30 ms CPU-budget timing reading in a package this diff does not touch. It was judged a flake in comment 6932525350 (with the package's local 1223/1223 at this head) and passed on its one re-run (job 133692293516).
  - Also `success`: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate (aggregate).
  - Local `dispatch-gates --ran`: 117/117, 0 NOT-MEASURED. That is a local subset only; the check-runs are the reading I used.
- **Dogfood battery** (owed: the title carries `!` and `Clause-②` carries `(narrowing)`). Card report 6932366621 reads: `7f731083 · os-verify-lock VERDICT command-exit 0 · Test Files 478 passed | 3 skipped (481) · Tests 4030 passed | 44 skipped (4074) · no failures`. It is pinned to this head and is the full package run; no red to fix or report.
- **Accepted deviations.**
  - (1) The dev ran the dogfood battery, where the delta said the seat would schedule it. The reading is head-pinned and full, so it counts.
  - (2) L2 N1: "it is not resolved" in the describes holds today for the hop shape only; a plain path still sends the list until #34389 lands. Lint refuses the path at every door and measured exposure is zero. Carried by #34389, accepted in the L2 record.
- **Out of scope.** The L2 record notes that a `$record` path to a structured field (json, repeater, location, address, vector) is not judged either. That is outside this card, with no carrier yet. The seat weighs whether to file it; it does not block this PR.

**L2 owed: yes, and it is in.** The surfaces touched are published schema (`packages/spec/src/**`, non-test) and narrowing, so the tier is `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Record 6932506491 (l2-review#4) carries `Served-tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` and `Head-sha: 7f7310830a0d4fa73576d316afafc25dbb134b2d`. That is the current head. It covers ①–④, has no must-fix or should-fix, one nit (N1, accepted), and reads **VERDICT: PASS**. Its `Scope:` covers every non-prose file in the diff. No `needs:contract-review` label is on the PR, which is right with a same-form PASS at this head.

**Landing tier.** `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34489` reads: "0 of 7 path(s) hit the register … ✅ NOT governed — ordinary queue landing applies"; 226 changed lines ≤ 3000. L1 ACCEPT and the L2 PASS are both on this head, and every check is green. The area lands it through the ordinary queue (ready → auto-merge). Per the area order, #34391 shares spec generated outputs: whichever of the two lands second runs `scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh` first.
